stories.headline: NBA opening day: Live updates, highlights from tripleheader
stories.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season is back with a bang. Follow along for all of the live updates and highlights from the tripleheader.
stories.body:
The NBA is back with a bang.

The 2026-27 season tips off with a tripleheader, beginning with a rare daytime game between the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics. That sets up ring night at Madison Square Garden as the New York Knicks host the Philadelphia 76ers. The night concludes with a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals between the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder.

Each game bring its own headlines, starting off in Detroit. The Pistons are coming off a 60-win season, while the Celtics debut the duo of Jayson Tatum and Paul George.

The Knicks are raising a banner for the first time in 50 years. Who will look to spoil their night? None other than the new-look 76ers, with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James teaming up with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Five months after defeating Oklahoma City in Game 7 to reach the Finals, San Antonio welcomes its Western Conference rivals in another battle. The Thunder and Spurs return most of their cores, setting up a matchup full of familiar matchups and tension.

We'll have all of the top moments and highlights from the NBA's tripleheader. Follow along below.

stories.headline: Champions League live updates: PSG, Barça share goals; Liverpool-Villarreal level
stories.summary: Follow live updates, scores and highlights from Tuesday's UEFA Champions League action, featuring PSG vs. Barcelona, Liverpool vs. Villarreal and more.
stories.body:
The Champions!

Another week, which means another round of European heavyweights facing off against each other.

The UEFA Champions League returned Tuesday for Matchday 3 of the league phase, with nine matches across the continent and plenty of mouthwatering clashes on the schedule.

Among the standout fixtures, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain welcomed Barcelona in a blockbuster showdown, and it lived up to the hype as the hosts won 4-2; Liverpool hosted Villarreal at Anfield, where the Reds were able to win 4-3, and Atlético Madrid traveled to Germany to face Stuttgart, where it ended in a 1-1 draw.

Elsewhere, Manchester City took on AEK Athens as the hosts won 5-1, while Napoli hosted Bodø/Glimt and ended up winning 4-3.

In our two early matches, we had Fenerbahçe and Slavia Prague facing off against each other as the match ended 2-2, and Sabah hosted Borussia Dortmund, where the German club got a 2-1 win away in Azerbaijan.

The other matches of the day included AS Roma beating Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and PSV Eindhoven were able to beat FC Porto 1-0.

stories.headline: Michael Carrick: I feel backing of Man United board but need to win games
stories.summary: Michael Carrick has said he feels the backing of the Manchester United board -- but admits it will only continue if he starts winning games.
stories.body:
COMO, Italy -- Michael Carrick has said he feels the backing of the Manchester United board -- but admits it will only continue if he starts winning games.

United, who face Como in the Champions League on Wednesday, are on a run of six games without a win.

- Fàbregas: Disrespectful to suggest I could replace Man United boss Carrick

- Who could replace Carrick after Man United's worst start since 1986?

- Ten Hag: Ronaldo let Man United down

A difficult start to the season has piled the pressure on Carrick with questions mounting about his future. And while the 45-year-old insists he has support of club chiefs, he accepts results need to change.

"I don't need any reassurance," Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday.

"It's pretty clear. I know the role, I know my responsibilities. I don't need anyone else to tell me that or tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better.

"I know that myself. I know the realities and I've got no problem with that. I know we've got to win football games for everything to flow and everything to fall into place. That's the great thing about it, you know? We can do something about it."

Asked specifically whether he feels the backing of minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, Carrick said: "Yeah, why wouldn't I?

"I'm in this position, I have a good relationship, a really good relationship with everyone, everybody at the football club. There's really no issues and no problems with any of that side. We've got to win games of football and that's what we're striving to do."

United are looking for their first away win in the Champions League since beating Villarreal in November 2021 when Carrick was interim boss following the sacking of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

With nine senior players injured, ill or suspended, Matthijs de Ligt could make his first appearance following an 11-month absence with a back injury.

"It's great to have him back," Carrick said of the Dutch defender.

"He's had such a long journey, being patient and he's worked hard. We're delighted to have him back. He's fit, he's ready, he's been training for a number of weeks now, so he's in a really good place."

Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martínez, Luke Shaw, Marcus Rashford and Ayden Heaven are among those who haven't made the trip to Italy. Leny Yoro is suspended after he was sent off in the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid last week.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey warning signs: D-men with hot starts to consider trading away
stories.summary: Sean dives into the defensemen trends to find warning signs for hot starters and what managers should do.
stories.body:
Last week, we looked at how little the early goalie standings tell you. Skaters aren't much easier to predict, but power-play time offers a useful clue. Especially for defensemen.

How many of the top 25 (by position) at this point of the season were still top-25 at the end:

2025-26: 10 forwards, nine defenders, 10 goalies

2024-25: 11 forwards, 11 defenders, 15 goalies

2023-24: 13 forwards, 16 defenders, 15 goalies

2022-23: 14 forwards, 12 defenders, 16 goalies

2021-22: 10 forwards, 10 defenders, 17 goalies

2020-21: 11 forwards, 13 defenders, 13 goalies

What the players who maintained their value averaged, compared with the ones who fell out (six-season averages):

Forwards who stayed: 4:00 PP TOI/GP, 0.59 blocks and 1.05 hits per game

Forwards who fell out: 3:21 PP TOI/GP, 0.61 blocks and 1.01 hits per game

Defenders who stayed: 2:48 PP TOI/GP, 2.06 blocks and 1.33 hits per game

Defenders who fell out: 1:58 PP TOI/GP, 2.05 blocks and 1.30 hits per game

Hits and blocks didn't separate them. Power-play time did, especially on the blue line. That puts these early leaders among defenders on watch:

MacKenzie Weegar, D, Utah Mammoth (available in 2.1% of ESPN leagues): fourth among defenders, 0:10 PP TOI/GP

Vladislav Gavrikov, D, New York Rangers (available in 32.3%): sixth among defenders, 0:04 PP TOI/GP

Travis Sanheim, D, Philadelphia Flyers (available in 30.8%): 10th among defenders, 0:14 PP TOI/GP

Declan Carlile, D, Pittsburgh Penguins (available in 57.5%): 12th among defenders, no PP time

Nick Seeler, D, Philadelphia Flyers (available in 84.6%): 16th among defenders, no PP time

Tyler Kleven, D, Ottawa Senators (available in 76.9%): 20th among defenders, 0:03 PP TOI/GP

Two weeks ago, this column called Gavrikov the easiest add of the early hits-and-blocks crowd. He has been worth it so far, but history says that kind of start rarely lasts without power-play time. Enjoy the blocks while they're paying off, just don't count on him staying sixth.

Among forwards, the stars clear the bar on talent alone. Connor McDavid averages 3:16 on the power play, and nobody is trading him. The ones to worry about are the passengers. Vasily Podkolzin ranks 11th among forwards, largely by riding with McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, and he gets 3:07 on the power play after finishing 107th last season. Artturi Lehkonen is 24th with just 1:48. If someone in your league is valuing their starts, this is the time to trade them away.

Hill is 4-0-0 with good starts (2.4 fantasy points or more) in three of four and ranks 10th in FPP60 (fantasy points per 60 minutes), and he and Hart have strictly alternated over the past four games. Vegas ranks fourth in team goalie fantasy points, and Hill is available in 83% of leagues, which makes him a cheap way into one of the league's best creases.

Nedeljkovic took two of three starts last week and ranks 12th in FPP60, while Askarov ranks 52nd and hasn't delivered a good start in his past three. The Sharks play five times in the next 10 days, and Nedeljkovic is available in 95% of leagues.

Last week, Tarasov was a speculative add. Two good starts in two tries later, he leads all goalies in FPP60, and the Red Wings have strictly alternated over the past four games. Calgary (30th in scoring) and Chicago (29th) are both on the schedule over the next 10 days.

Grubauer now has the better save percentage (.909 to .882) and FPP60 rank (24th to 35th), and with all four of Seattle's next games at home, he's the better bet in a true timeshare.

Levi is 4-1-0 with good starts in three of five, and his rostership has more than doubled in a week, yet he's still available in 68% of leagues. The Oilers' next five games are all at home, including Detroit (27th in scoring) and Calgary (30th), though Jarry has taken two of the past four starts.

Follow-ups from last week:

Dylan Garand, G, New York Rangers (available in 41.5%): Five straight starts and good starts in five of six overall. The Rangers play only three times in the next 10 days, but he shouldn't be on any waiver wire.

He has almost two weeks of runway left while Josh Morrissey is sidelined with a wrist injury.

Chandler Stephenson, C, Seattle Kraken (available in 91.6%): Two weeks ago, we doubted the Kraken's kids would keep the top unit. They didn't: Stephenson, Jordan Eberle, Jared McCann, Bobby McMann and Vince Dunn are back on it, and the group has scored four times in 16:30. Stephenson has two power-play points in his past three games.

Morgan Frost, C, Calgary Flames (available in 94.3%): The Flames' original top unit is back together after a brief swap, and Frost has two power-play points in his past three games with a 1.84 FPPG. Calgary plays twice this week and four times next week.

Ryan Leonard, RW, Washington Capitals (available in 65.9%): Leonard has held a top-unit spot alongside Alex Ovechkin for three straight games, playing 57 percent of the Capitals' power-play time, and he's at 1.91 FPPG.

Follow-ups from earlier columns:

Brayden Schenn, C/LW, New York Islanders (available in 77.2%): The Islanders' top unit has cooled since Simon Holmstrom replaced Matias Maccelli, and Schenn has no power-play points in his past three games. Hold off.

Kasperi Kapanen, RW, Edmonton Oilers (available in 94.8%): Zach Hyman is back on the top unit, and Kapanen is off it. That was quick.

Dmitry Orlov, D, San Jose Sharks (available in 88.1%): Orlov has taken over Luca Cagnoni's quarterback spot on the Sharks' top unit.

Droppables

Same caution as last week: this list flags rostered players whose production has lagged, and it still catches plenty of stars. Sidney Crosby (1.4 FPPG), Wyatt Johnston (1.4), Dylan Larkin (1.5), Artemi Panarin (1.7), Adrian Kempe (1.7), Mark Scheifele (1.7), Brayden Point (1.3) and Lucas Raymond (1.2) all qualify. All of them are on their team's top power-play unit, and none of them is going anywhere.

But as this week's intro showed, power-play time is what separates the players who hold their value from the ones who fade. These three have lost it:

Noah Dobson, D, Montreal Canadiens (rostered in 93.5%): Dobson is logging 21:33 a night but isn't on either power-play unit, because Lane Hutson runs both. That's a problem for a defender whose fantasy value has always leaned on the man advantage, and at 1.3 FPPG he's the clearest drop candidate on this list in standard leagues.

Dylan Cozens, C/RW, Ottawa Senators (rostered in 76.1%): Claude Giroux took Cozens' spot on the top power-play unit Friday, and Cozens was already at just 1.1 FPPG. He's movable in shallow leagues.

Morgan Rielly, D, Toronto Maple Leafs (rostered in 78.2%): Darren Raddysh has the top-unit quarterback job, and Rielly has been relegated to the second unit. At 1.2 FPPG, there are better defenders on most waiver wires, including a couple in this week's power-play section.

On notice:

Vincent Trocheck, C, Utah Mammoth (rostered in 87.6%): 16:18 a night, second power-play unit, 1.3 FPPG.

Alex Ovechkin, LW/RW, Washington Capitals (rostered in 88.9%): Still on the top power-play unit, but his 13:56 a night is the lowest ice time on this list, and he's at 1.0 FPPG.

stories.headline: Christian Horner opposed Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull move: 'Shouldn't have been promoted'
stories.summary: Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."
stories.body:
Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

The inexperienced Lawson was surprisingly picked to replace Sergio Pérez as Max Verstappen's new teammate in December 2024, but former team boss Horner says in his new autobiography, Drive, that he was uneasy with the decision and that it was Red Bull adviser Helmut Marko who pushed for the promotion.

Lawson was dropped after only two races, before Red Bull swiftly turned to Yuki Tsunoda.

"Liam was another racer from the junior programme and Helmut had championed the promotion, but I felt uncomfortable," Horner wrote.

"He was young and inexperienced, with only eleven Formula One races to his name, and we would be asking a huge amount from him."

Horner also accused Marko of playing political games over the decision, claiming the Austrian had told Lawson he was responsible for securing the drive.

"Meanwhile, Helmut was playing games," Horner wrote. "Before the final race of the season in Abu Dhabi, he had informed Liam that he would be driving for Red Bull because of his influence.

"When I challenged Helmut on this, he typically denied everything."

Lawson was promoted following Pérez's difficult 2024 campaign, which saw Red Bull finish third in the constructors' championship despite Verstappen winning his fourth consecutive drivers' title.

The New Zealander had impressed during two spells with the team's junior outfit but struggled immediately after stepping up to Red Bull.

He qualified 18th for the season-opening Australian Grand Prix before crashing out of the race, and then qualified last for both the sprint and the race in China.

"Liam only lasted two races," Horner wrote. "He struggled in pre-season testing and was clearly uncomfortable with the RB21's difficult handling characteristics.

"His confidence was smashed and, as with Pierre Gasly and Alex Albon, his arrival at Red Bull had come too soon.

"Sensing that the pressure on Liam was unfair, we replaced him."

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Horner said Honda, Red Bull's engine partner at the time, welcomed the decision to promote Japanese driver Tsunoda.

"The move back [to Racing] Bulls was tough for Liam," Horner wrote. "But he really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

Lawson returned to Racing Bulls, while Tsunoda remained alongside Verstappen for the rest of the 2025 season.

Horner was subsequently dismissed as Red Bull team principal and CEO in July 2025.

Lawson said earlier this year that Red Bull created a false narrative around the reasons behind his early exit from the team. The 24-year-old said he wasn't "mentally struggling" and that Red Bull had actually pushed him towards a "wild" setup change to find performance, which ultimately hampered his pace. He added that he now pretends in his mind he "never even went there."

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: ALEXIA PUTELLAS
This result is not a surprise. Putellas is the clear favourite for the award, and our voters agreed.

Putellas enjoyed a dream end to her 14-year Barcelona career last season, captaining the club to a second Quadruple in three years, including lifting the Women's Champions League, before she moved to captain London City Lionesses, who are now third in the Women's Super League after five games.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: NFL to increase security in Paris for Steelers-Saints game
stories.summary: The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Sunday after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend.

Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said officials are collaborating with Parisian and national authorities overseas, along with the U.S. State Department. League officials, including senior VP of security Cathy Lanier, have been on the ground in France, according to O'Reilly.

"There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security -- everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said at the league's annual fall owners meeting. "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams."

O'Reilly said there was never a point that the game was in danger of not being played at Stade de France, which is in the outskirts of Paris in Saint-Denis. He cited other sporting events ongoing in the city, including a Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona on Tuesday night.

The NFL has in the past moved games to avoid getting in the way of local response to an unforeseen event, and officials believe that is not an issue for the league's debut in France.

"We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. "That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."

Rioters clashed with police, set cars on fire, stormed public buildings and engulfed a historic city hall in flames in France's worst civil unrest in years as violence and looting swept through major cities.

About 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend, and authorities said thousands of businesses were damaged or looted. The rioting overshadowed demonstrations against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools in which hundreds of thousands of people marched peacefully.

The Saints traveled directly to Paris after playing at the New York Giants and are practicing in the area this week. The Steelers are set to travel closer to kickoff.

With the collective bargaining agreement allowing for up to 10 international games, O'Reilly said that number is being considered for next season. There are a record nine on the schedule this year.

Where those games take place is still being discussed.

"We like continuity, but we are looking at new regions, and Asia would be one of them," O'Reilly said.

After so much talk leading up to and coming out of the game in Melbourne, Australia, about the Los Angeles Rams waiting until late to fly there -- and lost 27-7 to San Francisco -- the NFL does not appear close to dictating when teams must travel.

"That is the discretion of the club," O'Reilly said. "As it stands today, you let the football decisions reside at the football level in terms of how they want to plan and prepare for a game coming in. That's not something we're ruling out, and there could be discussion on is there some standardization in the future. But right now, that's the prerogative."

With his suspension over Tuesday, 49ers owner Jed York was in attendance for the fall meeting.

York was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy after being arrested in a prostitution sting in Ohio in August. He pleaded no contest to two misdemeanors but was still punished by the league and stayed away from the 49ers during their 6-0 start.

York didn't attend the owners' meetings in Atlanta the week of his arrest.

stories.headline: Silver: LeBron's helicopter travel 'perfectly appropriate'
stories.summary: The helicopter used by Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James to commute from New York is "perfectly appropriate," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The helicopter used by 76ers forward LeBron James to commute to Philadelphia from New York is "perfectly appropriate," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday.

"He has a deal with Fanatics," Silver said. "It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're going to supply a helicopter to him as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved; there's no rules issue there whatsoever."

After signing with the Sixers in free agency, James decided to live in New York -- a decision Sixers players have made before him, including his former coach, JJ Redick -- but James' choice to travel by helicopter has made headlines.

During news conferences after practice, players often pause and laugh as James' helicopter is heard exiting from the roof of the team's business center, drowning out the sound in the facility.

James recently brushed off the added attention to his travel method.

"I've done it before; just another way of transportation," he said.

Brady Tkachuk expects an unruly reception as he returns to Ottawa for the first time on Wednesday, after the Senators traded him to the Florida Panthers in the offseason. But if any of his No. 7 Ottawa jerseys hit the ice in protest, Tkachuk has plans to use them for a good cause.

On his "Wingmen" podcast on Tuesday, Tkachuk said he spoke with the Panthers and "every jersey that gets thrown on the ice is going to get donated to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa."

While Tkachuk said he doesn't "recommend doing it," he does anticipate he might see some fans toss their jerseys on the ice in protest.

Tkachuk was traded in June after having told Senators management that he didn't intend to sign an extension when his contract is up in 2028. He used his no-movement clause to force a trade to the Panthers, joining his brother and podcast co-host Matthew Tkachuk in South Florida.

"Clearly, it was pointed at one team at the end," said Ottawa GM Steve Staios.

Tkachuk's departure was contentious among Ottawa fans, saying he was "fully committed" to the franchise back in April. His return to face the Senators on Wednesday will be the first chance for those fans to let their displeasure known.

"If you're going to do it and send a message, just know that it's going to a good cause. I've received your message," Tkachuk said.

Matthew Tkachuk said he would like to see "10,000 Tkachuk jerseys on the ice" on Wednesday night.

Brady Tkachuk said the Boys and Girls Club is a "special place" where he and his wife, Emma, forged many meaningful relationships during their time in Ottawa.

Tkachuk played 572 games over eight seasons with the Senators, who drafted him fourth overall in the 2018 NHL draft. He scored 213 goals with 250 assists, as well as 821 penalty minutes as a physical tone-setter for the team. He served as team captain for five seasons, succeeding Erik Karlsson.

"This is the game that's been circled. I'm going to assume I'm not the only one that's had it circled," he said. "The place is still special to me. Eight years. I've experienced so much. Became a father and a husband during my time there. They have such amazing people that makes that organization tick and I'm excited to see them."

Tkachuk said he expected to have dinner with some former Ottawa teammates on Tuesday night, organized by defenseman and Olympic gold medal teammate Jake Sanderson.

stories.headline: WNBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Dream the favorites after Game 2 win
stories.summary: The odds have shifted in the Dream's favor as the series moves to Atlanta for Game 3.
stories.body:
The Golden State Valkyries suffered a rare home loss at Ballhalla during Game 2 of the WNBA Finals and lost title favorite status as a result. The Atlanta Dream are now favored to win the franchise's first title at -135 after coming into the Finals as +105 underdogs, and the Valkyries are +115 after beginning the series at -125.

The Dream began the campaign with solid +650 odds to win the Finals, fourth on the odds board, but the Valkyries came in at a much longer 45-1, ninth on the board, in just their second season in existence.

The series shifts to Atlanta for Game 3 on Wednesday, with the home team a 3.5-point favorite and the total set at 151.5.

Despite her team falling behind in the series, Gabby Williams remains the favorite for Finals MVP at +125, with Angel Reese just behind at +225 after a massive 30-point, 16-rebound effort in Game 2. The next favorites for the award are Atlanta players Allisha Gray (+550), Jordin Canada (12-1) and Rhyne Howard (14-1), with Veronica Burton the next Valkyrie at 35-1.

Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.
